headline: Thousands gather in Dhaka as Argentina beats Algeria 3-0
summary: Fans at Dhaka University and 300 Feet road erupted in celebration after the defending champions' flying start to the World Cup.
details: Defending champions Argentina secured a dominant 3-0 victory over Algeria in their opening World Cup match.
The win sparked massive celebrations across Dhaka, with thousands of fans gathering to watch the game on giant screens.
Key gathering points included Dhaka University's TSC and Mohsin Hall grounds, where supporters cheered Lionel Messi's team.
Fans wearing team jerseys and waving flags filled the streets, including the 300 Feet road area, to celebrate the victory.
caption:
Argentina starts the World Cup with a bang! 🇦🇷

Thousands of Dhaka fans erupted in joy after a 3-0 win over Algeria.

Defending champions Argentina secured a dominant 3-0 victory over Algeria in their opening World Cup match.

The win sparked massive celebrations across Dhaka, with thousands of fans gathering to watch the game on giant screens.

Key gathering points included Dhaka University's TSC and Mohsin Hall grounds, where supporters cheered Lionel Messi's team.

Fans wearing team jerseys and waving flags filled the streets, including the 300 Feet road area, to celebrate the victory.

headline_marked: Tigresses suffer [[nine-wicket defeat against Australia]] in T20 World Cup
headline: Tigresses suffer nine-wicket defeat against Australia in T20 World Cup
summary: Bangladesh women's team posted their lowest-ever total against Australia, limping to 77/8 before the six-time champions chased it down in just 9.3 overs.
details: A woeful batting display condemned Bangladesh to a crushing nine-wicket defeat against Australia in their second Group A match of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup at Headingley in Leeds.
Asked to bat first, the Tigresses suffered an early collapse, slumping to 27 for five inside eight overs.
Captain Nigar Sultana Joty top-scored with 27 off 47 balls, while Ritu Moni added 16 from 26 deliveries in a brief 32-run resistance.
Bangladesh eventually limped to 77 for eight in their allotted 20 overs, marking their lowest-ever total against Australia in this format.
Australia made light work of the chase, reaching the target in just 9.3 overs with opener Georgia Voll remaining unbeaten on 45 off 32 balls.
The emphatic win lifts Australia to the top of Group A standings with four points from two matches.
Bangladesh, who started their campaign with a victory over the Netherlands, now sit third in the group with two points.
The Tigresses will next face Pakistan at The Rose Bowl in Southampton on June 20.
caption:
Lowest-ever total against Australia. The Tigresses suffer a crushing 9-wicket defeat in the T20 World Cup.

A woeful batting display condemned Bangladesh to a crushing nine-wicket defeat against Australia in their second Group A match of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup at Headingley in Leeds.

Asked to bat first, the Tigresses suffered an early collapse, slumping to 27 for five inside eight overs.

Captain Nigar Sultana Joty top-scored with 27 off 47 balls, while Ritu Moni added 16 from 26 deliveries in a brief 32-run resistance.

Bangladesh eventually limped to 77 for eight in their allotted 20 overs, marking their lowest-ever total against Australia in this format.

Australia made light work of the chase, reaching the target in just 9.3 overs with opener Georgia Voll remaining unbeaten on 45 off 32 balls.

The emphatic win lifts Australia to the top of Group A standings with four points from two matches.

Bangladesh, who started their campaign with a victory over the Netherlands, now sit third in the group with two points.

The Tigresses will next face Pakistan at The Rose Bowl in Southampton on June 20.
